meta.title: Ukrainian A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Ukrainian → English (see the Ukrainian, recall the meaning) and English → Ukrainian (see an English meaning, recall the Ukrainian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Ukraine certifies proficiency in the language but publishes no graded word list, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 442 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, jobs and study, clothes, more food and cooking, the rooms and furniture of a home, the town and its services, travel and holidays, nature, the seasons and the compass, animals, health and the body, feelings and character, free time, sport and holidays, telling what happened when, the higher numbers and measures, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing, cooking and doing — and the other 308 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Ukrainian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Cyrillic with its stress marked (кни́га, роблю́), because Ukrainian stress can fall on any syllable and move as the word changes, and nothing else shows it; there is no transliteration, and the Ukrainian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters. The 392 nouns show their gender, their genitive and their plural; the 192 verbs show their aspect, imperfective or perfective, with the other verb of the pair beside them, their я and він forms and their past; and behind the All forms fold every noun's seven cases and every verb's tenses by person. Real example sentences come with 745 of the 750 words, three apiece for 729 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, aspect, stress and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
